title: Building a House Budget from A to Z: The Costs Owners Must Count
desc: How to build a complete house budget: construction, design, supervision, procedures, equipment, furniture and contingency, with an example and tips.
summary: A guide for owners to list every cost group when building a house, how to calculate the contingency and how to keep the budget from blowing out midway.
body: p

Many families only ask “how much per square metre to build a house” and multiply by the floor area. That figure is usually only the construction cost, excluding design, procedures, equipment, furniture and extras. This article helps you build a complete budget table before calling a contractor.
h2
1. Why build a budget before calling workers?
p

For projects using state capital, the law requires determining a total investment consisting of several items: construction cost, equipment, project management, consultancy, other costs and contingency (Clause 1, Article 5 of Decree 206/2026/ND-CP). A household house is not required to follow it, but the Decree allows other projects to refer to the way these costs are determined (Clause 2, Article 2). The State's grouping is a very good framework so that owners do not miss anything.
h2
2. Group 1 - Construction cost
p

This is the largest item, covering the rough structure (foundation, frame, walls, roof) and the finishing (plastering, tiling, painting, electrics and plumbing, doors). Under the State's method, construction cost consists of direct costs (materials, labour, construction machinery), indirect costs, estimated taxable income, value added tax and the cost of temporary site-management housing (Clause 2, Article 12). When you receive a quotation, ask clearly whether these parts are fully included, especially tax, temporary accommodation and construction electricity and water.
h2
3. Group 2 - Design, supervision, procedures
ul

Design: a house of 3 or more floors, with a basement, with total floor area of 250 m² or more, or 12 m or higher must be designed by an organisation or individual with the relevant expertise (Clause 2, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP). See also Designing your own house: when must you hire a designer?

Supervision: the owner is responsible for organising construction, supervision and safety (Clause 3, Article 10). If you cannot supervise yourself, set aside an amount to hire a supervisor - see Is hiring a supervisor compulsory when building a house?

Procedures: applying for a building permit (if required), as-built completion and registering the house on the certificate, surveying and extracts. A house that a household or individual builds for themselves is exempt from the registration fee (Clause 11, Article 10 of Consolidated Document 33/VBHN-BTC).
h2
4. Group 3 - Equipment, furniture and other costs
p

Sanitary fittings, kitchen, water heater, air conditioning, pump, lights; kitchen cabinets, wardrobes, beds, curtains; gate, fence, yard, plants; cleaning, moving, the groundbreaking ceremony and housewarming. These items are usually outside the construction quotation but together can be very large. List each item room by room for a closer estimate.
h2
5. Contingency: how much to set aside?
p

The law does not set a contingency rate for private houses. State-funded projects include a contingency for additional quantities and price escalation (Point g, Clause 1, Article 5). For a house, many families set aside about 5-10% of the total budget as contingency; renovated houses and houses on weak ground should set aside more. This is a reference figure, not a mandatory level.
h2
6. An illustrative budget example
p

Assumption: a 3-floor townhouse, with the contractor quoting a full-package construction cost of VND 1.8 billion (an assumed figure for illustration, not a market price). The budget table could look like this:
ol
Construction cost per quotation: VND 1,800 million.
Design, supervision, procedures (assumed): VND 90 million.
Basic equipment and furniture (assumed): VND 300 million.
Gate, yard, moving, other costs (assumed): VND 60 million.
Contingency of 8% of the four items above: about VND 180 million.
Total budget to prepare: about VND 2,430 million - roughly 35% higher than the initial quotation figure.
h2
7. Tips to keep the budget from blowing out
ul
Finalise the design and the materials list before signing the construction contract.
Require the quotation to state its scope and whether taxes and fees are included (Clause 2, Article 11 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP).
Agree in writing on the price of every change and extra before doing it.
Record spending each week against the budget to spot an overrun early.
p
Need a detailed estimate for your own house? Contact Quan Construction for advice. See also What costs does a construction estimate include?
note

This article is for reference only and is not financial advice. The figures in the example are assumptions for illustration, not market unit prices; actual costs depend on the design, materials, location and time of construction. Decree 206/2026/ND-CP is mandatory only for state-funded and PPP projects; for private houses it is for reference only.
